Spotlight: Highly tried since debut win at Bath (5.7f, firm) in May; seemed to show improvement when sixth of eight in C&D Group 2 three weeks ago, although 50-1 and no threat; that run hasn't been missed by the handicapper.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Like Rollthedicebaby, she finished in mid-division in the Super Sprint (80-1) last time, but she had no excuses on account of the draw; up against it here from 4lb out of the handicap.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field in the Group 2 Queen Mary at Royal Ascot, but she'd previously come from the rear to win the Listed Marygate at York (5f, good); should be just as effective over 6f and may still have untapped potential.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Gained deserved win after three second places in maiden at Lingfield (6f, good to firm) 17 days ago, no more than workmanlike in landing the odds; in deeper here and 3lb out of weights but she may not be fully exposed.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Could finish only in midfield in the Super Sprint at Newbury (4-1) last month but she was done no favours by the draw; better judged on a clearcut maiden win at Goodwood (6f, soft) the time before; remains open to improvement and may well get back on track here.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Improving with each run and won going away from two rivals in nursery at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) 11 days ago; raised 5lb but should be well suited by this return to 6f and may well complete a hat-trick.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Has taken off for front-running tactics and cheekpieces on her last two starts, winning nurseries at Catterick and Thirsk (both 6f, good to firm); up 11lb in total but keeps improving and should make another bold bid.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Got up late on to win maiden at Chester (5.5f, good) in May but ran poorly when upped to 7f for nursery there two months later; perhaps this intermediate trip will suit but she's on a retrieval mission.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Kingman; sister to winners Calyx (6f including 2yo Group 2; RPR 118), Coppice (7f/1m including 2yo/Listed; 117) and Stanage (7f; 92); dam 6f-1m 2yo winner (including Group 3; 112), sister to 6f Group 1 winner African Rose; has an excellent Juddmonte pedigree and her stable's 2yos are just beginning to fire; big player on paper.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Quite stoutly bred and predictably improved for the step up to 7f when third here (good to firm; 33-1) two weeks ago; the type to progress with racing and should be involved in the shake-up once more.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 380,000gns yearling; by Dark Angel; dam 5f/5.5f winner (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 99), half-sister to 5f-6f winner Marching Mac, out of 1m winning half-sister to 7f Group 3 winner Muthabara; expensive purchase with a useful pedigree and representing a leading local yard.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Frankel; sister to 1m3f/2m2f Flat (RPR 84) and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner Secret Force, half-sister to 7f winner Cerro Blanco (103); dam 7f/1m winner (including 2yo/Listed; 107), out of Group-placed 7f 2yo winner; stable won this race in 2017, 2020 and 2024 and has a strike-rate of over 40% with its 2yos this season.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 200,000euros yearling; Coulsty half-sister to winners Pierre Bonnard (1m/1m2f 2yo including Group 1; RPR 119), Crepe Suzette (Group-placed 9.4f; 110) and Diavolo (7f; 91); dam 1m2f-1m4f winner (including Group 1 Nassau Stakes; 116); has a classy pedigree; stable's 2yos operating at 19% this season.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Stradivarius; dam placed 7f 2yo (RPR 70), half-sister to useful winners Not Never (1m1f 2yo/1m4f Flat and 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase) and Final Watch (7f); may be of more interest in the longer term.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Slowly away and always behind both starts; may benefit from today's step up in distance but needs a giant leap forward.

Campaigned over as far as 10.3f but proved well suited by the drop back to 7f when winning in clearcut style at Yarmouth (good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) last month; now that connections have found the key, she's open to further improvement; leading contender.
Likeable 7f specialist (all four wins at this trip); just edged out by Sierra Sands over C&D three weeks ago; holding his form really well and should be in the thick of things again.
Unlucky over this trip at Sandown two outings ago from just 1lb lower, but was disappointing when only fourth there next time; hasn't had much racing and may get back on the up.
Thriving on this course this summer, and beat Lion Of Mali a neck over C&D three weeks ago; edging up the weights only slowly and should give another good account of himself.
Sprang a 25-1 upset on debut at Newbury (6f) last summer, but unplaced all outings since, including over 1m4f last time; plummeting in the weights but hard to fancy.

Narrowly beaten on three of his four starts since being gelded, going down on the nod at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) on latest; should go close again off an unchanged mark, especially if first-time headgear has a positive effect.
Gained his most recent win here (1m6f) last August off 2lb lower in first-time blinkers; with creditable shows in two of his three starts this season, he is firmly in calculations.

Has done well over 1m4f-1m6f on turf this term, winning three times from six starts; latest win came easily at this track (1m6f, good to firm) in June and he's 7lb higher today; tailing off so badly at Southwell four weeks ago may be offputting but he came last in 2025 in his only other AW race, so perhaps can spring back to life with today's return to turf.

Ten-time AW winner who is 5lb lower than when winning at Southwell (1m4f, AW) last November; however, this is his first run since January and he was well beaten at Ascot in May 2024 on his last encounter with turf; 0-5 on grass and others have less to prove.

Often ridden by claimer Alexandra Egan, including when he won a four-runner C&D race (good to firm) last July off the same mark as today; creditable second on last two outings (C&D latest) suggest he will be bang there.

5yo now who won for Sean Woods on belated debut last July; no joy in his seven races since, three for this yard, but he kept on well for a good third of 12 in a slowly run race at Ayr (upped markedly to 1m5f, soft) in June and may well have been stretched by 1m6f when performing respectably at Ascot (good to firm; made most) three weeks ago; firmly in the mix.

He's had a long career but never been better than this season, winning on AW at Wolverhampton (9.4f) and Lingfield (1m4f); they were in March/April but he returned from a break with creditable third of six here (1m2f, good to firm) 15 days ago, again under Olivia Tubb; probably not far away.

Both wins (from nine races) have been in small fields, including from off the pace at Lingfield (1m2f, good to firm) on reappearance ten days ago; going back up 4lb demands more but there's a fair chance that he'll turn out to be an improved performer this term; up 2f, which he's not sure to stay, but he has to be on the shortlist.

OwnerName: S Mizon, H McAlpine & Winner Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Has some back-class but now 0-11 for this yard and the form he showed in initial outings last summer has not been repeated; accelerating down the weights, which gives him a chance on this year's form even, but others are more convincing.

280,000gns purchase as a yearling; hasn't gone on as anticipated from a promising debut, fading and beating only one home in maiden at Yarmouth (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago; still early days but she has something to prove.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Has taken a while to get the hang of things, but improved form last two starts, winning novice in small field at Nottingham and pulling clear with the winner when second in handicap at Salisbury (both 1m2f, good to firm); tactically versatile and looks the one to beat.
6f winner last autumn; has been running respectably in 7f/1m handicaps without looking ahead of her mark; now moves up in distance (sister won up to 1m2f); should be thereabouts.
Two wins from ten outings, both over the extended 1m at Nottingham; faded on first attempt at 1m2f when fifth at Windsor last time; beginning to look exposed.
Tough 5f performer, holding his form well; close third under regular rider Chloe Lyons at Windsor on Monday; should give it his best shot again.

Lightly raced 3yo; sole win came over this trip at Southwell last winter, and she shaped nicely after six months off on turf debut at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; now fitted with a tongue-strap; big player if building on her last run.

0-7 on the AW between September and April, but he has won his last five races on turf; patiently ridden as usual and led late at Brighton (5f, good to firm) six weeks ago; edging up the weights only slowly and in the mix once more.
Missed 2025 but is making up for lost time and completed a hat-trick of 5f handicaps at Salisbury (good to firm) 11 days ago; thriving and may not have reached her limit just yet.

0-7; never dangerous when sixth of 11 on stable debut at Windsor (5f, good to firm) on Monday, finishing three places behind Merrimack; however, she did meet trouble that day and can't be ruled out entirely.
Started well for this yard but seems to have gone off the boil, safely held when fourth over C&D two weeks ago; needs a revival.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Never looked like getting to Palm Reader when second at Beverley (5f, good to firm) four weeks ago; no improvement for stepping up to 6f at Hamilton two weeks ago; 7lb turnaround in the weights may be insufficient to turn the tables.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 92,000gns yearling; second foal; half-brother to 7f AW winner Espona Bay (RPR 71); dam 5f 2yo winner (89), half-sister to 7f winners Bendy Spirit and The Toff; stable operating at a healthy strike-rate with 2yos this season; betting useful.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Never in the hunt in a 5f novice at Newcastle five weeks ago (18-1); should do much better at some point.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Unique Retreats, P Morrall & J Blackburn
Spotlight: Cost 160,000euros at the breeze-ups in May; justified favouritism with a front-running success at Beverley (5f, good to firm; Battle Fever second) four weeks ago; more to come and he's the one to beat.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 150-1 when finishing down the field on last week's Newcastle debut (6f, AW); needs a big step forward.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd
Spotlight: 33-1 and always in rear on his debut at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 12 days ago; best watched.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Modest form in two 5f maidens 98 days apart (gelded after debut); improvement essential.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Down the field in two 5f runs last month; minor nurseries beckon.
Formerly smart but is currently out of sorts, as several duck eggs next to his name reflect, and hasn't scored on turf for nearly three years (gained last two wins on Newcastle AW); opposed.

Formerly a miler but has gained last three wins over 1m2f, the most recent in Bahrain; well held in major handicap returned to home soil last time; bit to prove off current mark back down in trip; Lexie Clarkson claims 7lb but has limited experience.

Nosed ahead in the final strides at York (7f) last time, ending a two-year losing spell and showing he retains plenty of ability aged eight; back up just 2lb he remains well treated on historical data; won the Thirsk Hunt Cup over C&D in 2023; should remain competitive.

Sole 3yo in this field; maiden last term; gelded prior to posting form figures of 131 (over 7f-1m) this season, the wins on sharp, left-handed tracks, namely Catterick (good) and Chester (good to soft); open to further improvement, should take well to Thirsk and receives weight all round; respected.

Commenced career with two wins, including Listed; 0-6 and patchy form-wise since but proved resurgent in York handicap (1m; debut for new stable) most recently and is interesting off current mark assuming he builds on that effort.

Record of 3-11 in France for Henri-Francois Devin, most recently prevailing narrowly in big-field handicap at Longchamp in May; sold for 80,000euros since; likely faces a stiffer task off opening British mark but market support should be heeded.

Campaigned mostly at the Newmarket tracks this term, winning in May and respectable third last time; has shown versatility in the past but looks weighted to the hilt off current mark and this step back up in class adds to the difficulty.

Scored twice in 2024 and three times in 2025; gradually back to form this season, creditable second in useful handicap at York (1m) most recently; appears to be on his way to regaining the winning thread and looks a must for the shortlist.

Useful on his day and has a record of 2-3 over C&D, notably a success off current mark in this year's Thirsk Hunt Cup; not particularly solid on form elsewhere since but the return to this scenario may have a positive effect; not dismissed.

Generally in good form, mostly on AW, for current stable and latest effort is best forgiven (race didn't pan out favourably); not disgraced in most recent turf attempt but is still seeking a first success in this sphere and is somewhat hostage to fortune the way he races.

Front-running tactics backfired at the Newmarket July festival last time when bidding for a 1m hat-trick after Class 4 wins at Carlisle; remains on career-high mark and is upped further in grade, so needs to resume his improvement.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has shown promise in both starts, even when last of three at Chester (1m2f, good) last month (runner-up has won since); shortlisted for stable that took this in 2022 and 2023.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 450,000gns yearling; disappointing when sent off favourite for his Salisbury debut (7f, soft) in June, but with a tongue-tie fitted he showed his true colours when winning a Kempton novice (7f, AW) last month; has a 7lb penalty to carry, but bred to be smart so could easily step forward again.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Huge prices and failed to beat a rival in his first two starts (7f/1m2f) eight months apart; handicaps beckon.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Offered promise when fourth of ten in a Doncaster maiden (1m, soft) on his debut September, but well held on his Hamilton return (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago; looks one for handicaps.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sent off 100-1 when beaten miles into last of 13 on his Southwell debut (7f, AW) nine days ago; stable runs three.

OwnerName: Miss K Padgett And Mrs S D Pearson
Spotlight: Well handicapped on this winter's AW form but he has gone off the boil more recently; given a chance by the handicapper as a consequence and he needs a market check starting out for Ruth Carr (sold out of David Loughnane's stable for 22,000gns last month).
Successful off this mark at Wolverhampton in March; solid efforts on his last three starts and he should make a bold bid to win this race for the second season in succession.

Won a 5f handicap off this mark at Newmarket (good to firm) last August; she has run some fair races this year but her latest effort (tried in cheekpieces, usual visor back on today) wasn't one of them; no surprise to see her bounce back quickly.

Prominent racer; thriving this season, winning three of his last five starts with the latest a cosy success at Hamilton (5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; up 4lb but he needs serious consideration; stable also runs American Bay.
C&D winner; below par in a big field at York (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago but plenty of form this season that makes him of interest; Jack Callan's claim a bonus; one to consider back at 5f.
5f AW win in April; ran well at Ripon (5f, good) later that month but he has struggled twice since; has a C&D win on his record but others bring more pressing claims.
Two 5f wins this year and she ran her best race so far when third of 12 at York (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; races off the same mark here and should make another bold bid.
Three wins in 5f handicaps this year, the latest off 6lb lower last month; another good effort when second over 6f here last week; likely vulnerable in Class 4.
Wasn't winning out of turn when taking a 5f handicap at Wolverhampton in May; didn't get the clearest run at Chester three weeks ago but that took his turf record to 0-11; others are more appealing.
Didn't run badly at Windsor in May but that run is sandwiched by two lesser turf runs; connections now turn to a tongue tie and cheekpieces.
Has a couple of C&D wins on his record; not found his best form this year and he has too much to prove for comfort, for all he is tumbling down the weights.
Talented veteran but has temperament to match his ability; no turf win since 2021 and when second at Nottingham 11 days ago there were only four runners; more minor money perhaps his best hope.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Impressive on 2yo debut in 2024 (6f, good) then absent until last month, when going very close at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) before easy win at 1-50 at Lingfield (6f, good to firm); could be on a good mark for this first handicap.
Won at Lingfield (1m, AW) in April and achieved his best result of this turf season when close fourth of 17 at York (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago; he might not be far away.
Well handicapped on his form up to June 2023 but he was then absent until this season and hasn't been the force of old on his three runs in 2026.

Without a win since August 2024 but he's been in good form since this visor went on, bumping into an unexposed 3yo when second of four at Catterick (7f, good to firm) and again finishing runner-up at Chester (7.5f, good) last time; in each-way calculations once more.

Ran really well when runner-up in two big-field handicaps at York (7f/1m, good) in June; not at the same level when mid-division there (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces (retained) but can be in the shake-up if swiftly rediscovering his previous form.

Won over C&D (good) in May and close second at Chester (7f, good) a fortnight later; respectable sixth of 19 at York (7f, good) next time and perhaps unsuited by return to AW most recently; each-way possibilities.

Well beaten on final outing last season and same story on reappearance at Epsom on Oaks day (pulled hard); he has something to prove but that latest outing may have got the freshness out of him and he's on a handy mark on last season's best efforts; not written off.

Four-time AW winner, the latest at Newcastle (7f) in May, and good second at Chester (7f, good to soft) in June; however, only fifth of ten at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last time and has to leave that run behind if he's to get off the mark on turf at the seventh attempt.

8yo who was knocking on the door prior to making all in fine style at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) 12 days ago; had just three rivals to beat last time and he's 4lb higher in a tougher race today, but is clearly in good heart and is a two-time winner at Thirsk; could go well.
She's dropped below her last winning mark and has run some reasonable races on turf this summer, but without suggesting a win is imminent; she's just 1-20 on grass as opposed to 6-43 on AW.

Reappeared at York (7f, good) in June following a wind op and he beat 19 rivals to win; very much of interest based on that performance but he was well beaten back at York (7f, good to firm) last time; cheekpieces go on.
Won at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) in May and has run well in defeat at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) and Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) on his last two starts; he's in with an each-way chance.

OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd & Julie Camacho
Spotlight: Won in fields of a similar size to today's at York (7f, good) last July and Wetherby (7f, good to firm) in June; outside of those wins his form figures since last June read 000089055 and he's a type who needs everything to drop right, but it's possible that will happen off an expected good pace today.

Very lightly raced since winning two 2yo novice races in autumn 2024 (7f, AW); returned from another absence at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in April, having been gelded, and ran well in second of six; could have part to play.

Won four times in 2024; just two runs last year and reappeared this April with close third at Redcar; down to a dangerous mark but he hasn't really shone on his last four starts and has to turn things around.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Improved form the last twice, finishing first past the post at Goodwood (1m4f; demoted to second for causing interference) then beaten only a neck at Newbury (1m5f); respected.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Novice win last October; has come up well short in Class 4 handicaps this term (modest fourth last time; gelded since) but may fare better off a reduced mark at this lower level.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Five-race maiden who has two standout pieces of form, including creditable effort with cheekpieces fitted at Doncaster (1m4f) last time; could go well in the retained headgear.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Exposed 6yo who concedes weight to 3yo rivals but brings positives, being the only C&D scorer in the field and a winner off 2lb higher in most recent attempt in this grade.
Not beaten far on a few occasions in the spring, but now 0-12 and cheekpieces made no difference last time; needs the addition of a tongue-tie to make a difference.

Very disappointing at Ascot (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago which needs forgiving, but his Chepstow success (7f, good to firm) in May was the only occasion he has dropped into Class 6 company in more than two years; worth a second look.

Narrowly bounced back to winning form under Jonathan England at Carlisle (6f, good to firm) last month, but met traffic when fifth of ten at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 11 days later; a player granted better luck.

OwnerName: Mrs K S Pratt & M Dods
Spotlight: Handy sort whose three turf wins have all come over C&D; not firing of late, but has become dangerously well handicapped having dropped 14lb below his last winning mark.

2-6 over C&D; ended a 17-race losing run at Chester (7f, good) last month and only beaten just over 2l into fourth of eight at Catterick (7f, good to firm) ten days ago; shouldn't have an issue with the return to this trip and shortlisted.

Winner of eight races including one over C&D, but losing run up to 12 despite a slipping mark; not disgraced when fourth of 11 behind Great at Carlisle (6f, good to firm) last month, but he could really do with the ground easing.

OwnerName: P C J Dalby & R D Schuster
Spotlight: Both wins came on the AW last autumn; 1lb lower than for the latest, but he has beaten just one rival in four starts on turf; blinkers removed after one use and are replaced by cheekpieces.

0-9; 33-1 when second of 11 at Redcar (7f, good to firm; first-time tongue-tie) in May, but ran poorly over the same C&D the following month; has questions to answer back in trip; stable also runs Lord Abama.
Well handicapped on old form, but has shown little in two starts since returning from a long absence in May; just 1-36 on turf and hard to fancy.

Spotlight: Progressive turf performer, thriving at present and still not fully exposed; completed hat-trick in Listed race at Churchill Downs (1m3f) last time, beating smart Chapman's Peak (who received 5lb) by a neck, pair clear; previously wide-margin winner over 1m4f of Grade 2 at Keeneland and Grade 3 at Churchill Downs; the coming force in this division and can prove himself at top level today.

OwnerName: Epic Horses LLC, WSS Racing Et Al
Spotlight: Chilean Grade 1 winner in 2025; very useful form to complete hat-trick outside graded events in USA (one at Santa Anita, two at Gulfstream); on latest start (second for current trainer) he justified favouritism by just over 1l in handicap at Gulfstream (8.5f) from stablemate Nemo; progressive and in excellent hands but needs to rediscover peak from former country if he's to contend.

Smart and consistent type who has won three Grade 3s on Tapeta at Woodbine, including Autumn Stakes (1m1f) last November; showed himself just as good on turf (won allowance in May) when about 1l third to Lagynos in Grade 2 Wise Dan at Churchill Downs (8.5f) last time; best form at about 1m.
Grade 3 winner at Gulfstream Park (1m4f; good ride by David Egan) in January; better of two efforts since when fourth in Grade 3 on penultimate start but overall form leaves him plenty to find.

Last year's winner when he came off fast pace to beat Grand Sonata by half a length, with Integration close third; has struggled to reproduce that form, though did win Grade 3 Dinner Party Stakes (1m1f) at Laurel in May; respectable effort latest and maybe this track suits him, but on balance he looks opposable.

Benefited from excellent ride from Manny Franco when winning Grade 1 Pegasus World Cup Turf Invitational at Gulfstream in January (1m1f, firm) by a neck; back to form when beaten half a length by Deterministic in Grade 1 Manhattan Stakes (9.5f) at Saratoga; best form at shorter than 1m2f but should get the trip.

OwnerName: West Point Thoroughbreds & Woodford Racing LLC
Spotlight: Six wins from 18 starts include Grade 2s in 2023 and 2024; largely consistent since (close third in this last year) and beaten just under 2l by Deterministic when fifth in Grade 1 Manhattan Stakes (9.5f) at Saratoga on last start; looks poised to make a bold bid.

OwnerName: Wessel Thoroughbreds, R H Morrison Et Al
Spotlight: Let-up (42-days). Performance just fair in the Eye Liner at Ipswich when went around $10. Since trialled at Caulfield Heath 16 Jul. Each way claims.
Just missed in a crackerjack finish in the (Bm88) at Flemington over this trip. Can play a role.

OwnerName: Ms J McAlpine, Philippa Duncan Bloodstock Et Al
Spotlight: First-up (18-weeks). Last prep was highlighted by a G1 placing. Proven fresh performer. Has form this track and distance and a nice weight drop. Worth a look.

OwnerName: Lindsay Park Bloodstock Pty Ltd, P B Devitt Et Al
Spotlight: Turned on the speed and fended off challengers to narrowly prevail this course 4 Jul. Unbeaten at track and distance. Well placed for a repeat performance.

OwnerName: Seymour Bloodstock, B W James Et Al
Spotlight: Freshened. Not disgraced in soft going at Sunshine Coast. Switching to 1200m. Can challenge.

OwnerName: J P M Ma, A K Y Leung & Mrs J R McGrath
Spotlight: Resuming (39-weeks). Very speedy type. Nabbed on the wire in Open company first-up last campaign while warmed up with a synthetic trial & winning a recent Cranbourne jump-out. Watch closely.
Great run at Swan Hill 5 Jun. Made the running but soon off the bit and weakened noticeably this course last time. Drops back in trip now. Could run into the exotics.

OwnerName: Mailbag Windstorm, C C F C Group Et Al
Spotlight: Now 5 weeks between runs. Well back and never sighted at Caulfield at first run for new trainer at long odds. Usually gets back. Keener on others here.
